title: New model: TenantUsageCounter, maintained when the work happens
description:
Outcome: Per-tenant meters are counters, never counts made by reading tables. TenantUsageCounter: id "<tenant>#<meter>#<period>" (period = the Prospectus week start YYYYMMDD, or a UTC day for daily meters), tenantId, meter, period, value (integer, in the meter's unit), lastOperationId, updatedAt; index tenantId sorted by period. Every writer adds with one atomic UpdateItem ADD at the moment the work happens, with the operation id kept to make a retry harmless. Read by the newsroom usage panel and by the daily report to Prospectus (PPY-49d059). Model spend authority stays in Prospectus's quota; this table is Papyrus's local view and the source for shared-resource attribution.

Touches (verified at origin/develop 23fabe1d): amplify/data/schema.ts, src/papyrus_content (new usage module), lib/ twin for the newsroom panel.

Acceptance (Gherkin feature file: features_backend/tenant-usage-counters.feature):
Scenario: One unit of work adds once
    Given "alpha" publishes one story
    When the publish is retried with the same operation id
    Then the pages-written meter for this week rose once

Scenario: Showing usage reads only the tenant's counters
    Given 50 tenants with counters
    When "alpha"'s usage panel opens
    Then one query on the tenantId index runs

Dependencies: blocked by PPY-31c45c. Blocks PPY-3fd951, PPY-f40a02. (Also recorded as kbs dependencies.)
Implements or extends: PPY-ea3f08.

Testing: pytest with a DynamoDB fake; request meter assertion.
Rollout: Releasable alone.
Risk and mitigation: Risk: hot key on a busy meter. Mitigation: per-period rows, and high-volume meters (AppSync requests) are batched in memory per invocation before one ADD.

Releasable on its own: yes.
DynamoDB index: new table only: TenantUsageCounter (tenantId + period).
AppSync authorisation: changes: new model (tenant admin read, functions write).
Design note: docs/plans/multi-tenant-architecture.md (PR on branch docs/multi-tenant-architecture).
